articles.title: Toddler found with loaded handgun at daycare, parents expected to face charges
articles.summary: No injuries were reported.
articles.body:
Two parents are expected to face charges after a toddler was found with a loaded, holstered handgun inside his Michigan daycare, officials said.

A teacher noticed the gun Monday morning and took "immediate action," Canton Police Chief Joseph Bialy told ABC Detroit affiliate WXYZ. Officers then responded to the incident in Canton, just outside of Detroit, and secured the weapon, according to Canton police.

The Canton Public Safety Department said the toddler's parents are scheduled to be arraigned on Thursday. The charges are not clear and have not yet been formalized; the Wayne County Prosecutor's Office said a judge is expected to authorize the charges Thursday morning.

"The message here is that no matter how busy our lives are, we have a great responsibility if we're going to choose to own a firearm," the chief told WXYZ.

Children's World said in a statement, "There is nothing we take more seriously than the safety, security and well-being of the children entrusted to our care. We understand the concerns this event has caused our families, and as educators and parents ourselves, we fully share those feelings."

"We are proud of the immediate response our teachers took to ensure the safety of our children and are grateful that nobody was harmed," the statement continued. "... Effective immediately, we are introducing additional measures, including checking backpacks."

articles.title: Meet Aditya Herekar and Karan Verma, the US students who built a biodegradable coffee pod and won $25,000
articles.summary: A chemistry class assignment about household rubbish took two American high-school students into a problem that usually sits well outside the school
articles.body: A chemistry class assignment about household rubbish took two American high-school students into a problem that usually sits well outside the school curriculum. Aditya Herekar, from Edison, New Jersey, and Karan Verma, from Frisco, Texas, began looking at what happens to a coffee capsule after it has been used. Their work eventually led to a new pod material, a patent application and a published research paper. The pair developed Naturista, a coffee capsule made from pullulan, a food-grade polysaccharide that can dissolve or biodegrade instead of leaving behind a conventional plastic shell. Their project also reached the Mott Million Dollar Challenge, where the students won $25,000 for their work.How the founders turn a school waste project into a coffee pod ideaAs reported in Naturista, the idea began with a chemistry assignment focused on household waste. Coffee pods quickly became the subject because their construction presented a particularly awkward disposal problem. Conventional capsules can contain several bonded layers, including plastic and aluminium. The materials are designed to keep coffee protected during storage and brewing, but that combination also makes the used capsule difficult to process through ordinary household recycling. For Herekar and Verma, the question became less about how consumers should dispose of the pods and more about whether the pod itself needed to be made differently.They were also familiar with the product from their own homes. The project was not based solely on something they had read about in a textbook. It became an attempt to rethink an everyday object they were already using.How 200 prototypes helped turn a school project into materials researchThe early development work took place using equipment and materials they could obtain themselves. They ordered biopolymers, made moulds and cast films, then tested the resulting structures with coffee and hot water. Many of the early versions failed. Some did not retain their shape, while others could not withstand the conditions needed for brewing.The pair eventually arrived at a pullulan-based formulation that behaved differently. After roughly 200 prototypes, they produced a version that could maintain its structure through a complete extraction before breaking down when required.Pullulan became the material behind NaturistaPullulan is a polysaccharide produced by microorganisms and has applications in food and pharmaceutical products. Herekar and Verma were interested in its ability to form films while also being water soluble and biodegradable. The concept was relatively simple, even if making it work was not. A coffee capsule needs to survive a short period of heat, water and pressure. Once the coffee has been brewed, however, there is little reason for the shell to remain intact.The students looked towards bioabsorbable materials used in medicine for inspiration. Those materials are designed to provide structural support for a particular period before breaking down, removing the need for a later procedure to take them out.They applied a similar principle to packaging. Instead of making a coffee pod that could survive for years, they wanted one that would last only as long as the brewing process required.University experts helped turn the early prototypes into a productThe kitchen experiments eventually reached the point where specialist knowledge was needed. The founders began working with university professors with expertise spanning materials science, food science and shelf-life considerations. That assistance helped move Naturista beyond the prototype stage. The work expanded into questions that a kitchen experiment could not answer on its own, including how the material could perform consistently and what would be required to turn the concept into a commercially viable product.The project has since included a patent application and a published paper, giving the two students a body of work that extends beyond the original classroom assignment.Two versions are being developedNaturista's concept is not limited to one type of coffee capsule. The machine version is designed around the dimensions of a conventional single-serve pod. The intention is that consumers could use it with an existing machine rather than buying a new brewing system. The pullulan shell is intended to withstand the brewing cycle before being disposed of through home composting. Instead of entering a coffee machine, the pod is placed directly into hot water. Its shell dissolves and releases the coffee, leaving no conventional capsule behind.The two designs approach the same packaging problem differently. One is intended to fit into an established brewing routine, while the other removes the need for a machine altogether.The students say the problem is bigger than disposalNaturista's own research into coffee capsules points to the scale of the market. The company cites an industry estimate of more than 80 billion coffee pods being produced annually, with conventional capsules commonly combining plastic and aluminium.The founders also point to research published in 2025 that detected microplastic particles in samples of hot retail coffee. As reported by Naturista, the study tested 155 samples, with polypropylene among the polymers identified. That finding is part of the wider discussion around plastic contact with food and drinks, although it does not by itself establish that conventional coffee pods are responsible for all of the particles detected.The students' proposed alternative is therefore based on changing the material rather than asking consumers to alter what they do with the used capsule.Two students brought different interests to NaturistaAditya Herekar, a high-school student in Edison, New Jersey, developed an interest in sustainability and materials science while balancing school journalism, DECA and student council. He also co-founded Invest2Empower with Karan Verma, a student-led financial literacy initiative, and has volunteered as an English tutor.Verma, a high-school student in Frisco, Texas, shares Herekar’s interest in entrepreneurship through DECA, BPA and Invest2Empower. He has also volunteered at a local chef academy and served on a congressional youth advisory council. Their different interests came together through Naturista and its focus on rethinking disposable coffee packaging.The $25,000 prize put Naturista in the spotlightThe pair presented their work at the Mott Million Dollar Challenge, a competition that brought their prototype before judges outside the school environment. Their Naturista project ultimately won $25,000. For the students, the prize provided recognition for a project that had started with experiments on household waste and gradually developed into a more serious research and commercialisation effort.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tel Aviv flight passengers sprang into action after pilot stabbed copilot: Officials
articles.summary: Israeli officials alleged the suspect tried to bring down the jet.
articles.body:
Passengers aboard a FlyDubai flight to Tel Aviv on Wednesday sprang into action after a pilot allegedly stabbed another and plunged the plane thousands of feet in an apparent attempt to crash it, in what Israeli officials are saying was an act of terror.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the intention was to "crash the plane, killing everyone on board" Flight 1073 from Dubai.

Passengers described a violent mid-air incident as the unidentified pilot allegedly stabbed the other pilot, later identified by the prime minister as Capt. Smit Machchhar, in the cockpit.

"We just heard screams, and they opened the cockpit and saw amounts of blood from someone who had simply tried to murder the pilot and stabbed him with a pocketknife. Then the plane lost control," a passenger who identified herself as Miriam told Israeli media.

"We felt like we were, like, going to crash. I was already screaming, 'Shema Israel'," she added, referring to the Jewish prayer. "I can't die, I'm my only daughter, I can't do this to my mother."

Netanyahu said in a statement that the plane "went into a spin and began to dive." The passengers were predominantly Israeli citizens, he noted.

The prime minister said that even though Machchhar, who is from India, had been stabbed, he "fought back, resisted [and] opened the cockpit door."

Netanyahu said that some passengers took a stand, referring to one he said he spoke with after the incident.

"He managed to break into the cockpit with one of the crew members, and together they subdued the pilot who had committed the stabbing while he was attempting to sabotage the aircraft's systems," Netanyahu said.

"Another flight crew member on board entered the cockpit and managed to stabilize the plane," he added.

The flight landed in Tabuk, in northwestern Saudi Arabia, after being diverted.

"I salute the heroes on the flight from Dubai who demonstrated resourcefulness and courage. I have instructed the security establishment to prepare for potential additional threats," Netanyahu said in a statement.

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz also praised the passengers who stepped up and noted in his statement that investigation is still ongoing.

"According to our preliminary information, the terrorist had a single objective: to crash the plane, killing everyone on board," he said.

Machchhar was being treated for his injuries in Saudi Arabia and the suspect was detained, according to Israeli officials.

Attorney General Todd Blanche and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters that the U.S. is "closely coordinating with their counterparts overseas," stressing there are "no credible threats."

The flight took off at 7:05 a.m. local time from Dubai, according to Flightradar24.

Tracking data showed the aircraft descended rapidly from 34,000 to 16,000 feet in three minutes.

"It was the full like cabin, like cabins opening and everything, like chaos screaming and just the crazy drop. Like you look at the ground and you're like, OK, I'm going that way right now," Mika Bauman, a passenger, told ABC News.

"I think now I can go on every roller coaster and be fine after that because that was an insane drop," Bauman added.

About 10 minutes after the initial descent, the plane's squawk code -- used by aircraft to communicate with air traffic control -- changed to "general emergency." Seven minutes after that, the squawk code changed again, indicating a hijacking or "unlawful interference."

The aircraft then continued to fly lower at 15,000 feet on average until it landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, about an hour to an hour and a half after the rapid descent began and the emergency signals were sent.

FlyDubai confirmed that the flight "experienced an incident while en route," and landed in Tabuk.

One passenger expressed gratitude that the incident was resolved.

"We jumped and helped the pilot. Friends, everything is OK now, as you can see we are landing in Saudi Arabia, you can see I am fine. That's it. We will see in a few minutes what will happen when we land," Itzhak Liber, a passenger, said in a video he posted on Facebook.

An Israeli security source confirmed to ABC News that the Israel Defense Forces recommended that a military aircraft be sent to repatriate Israeli passengers from Saudi Arabia.

However, the Saudi government refused to allow an IDF rescue flight to bring back the Israeli passengers, two Israeli sources familiar with the matter told ABC News.

The repatriation flight landed on Wednesday evening local time, Israeli emergency services said.

"From first assessment, it appears nobody is going to need any medical treatment but we will assess them once more once they're in the terminal," an agency spokesman said.

At the airport, Netanyahu met with one of the passengers who subdued the suspect.

ABC News' Victoria Beaule, David Brennan, Gaby Vinick and Dana Savir contributed to this report.

articles.title: Kathua fratricide: Plaint over bringing child to project site enraged killer
articles.summary: JAMMU: The CISF jawan who shot dead four colleagues, including an assistant commandant, at an NHPC hydel plant in J&K’s Kathua district had allegedly got
articles.body: JAMMU: The CISF jawan who shot dead four colleagues, including an assistant commandant, at an NHPC hydel plant in J&K’s Kathua district had allegedly got into a heated argument with one of the victims over bringing his child to the project site, police said Wednesday.The accused head constable, Abhidesh Kumar Singh of Bihar, was remanded in seven-day police custody. DG (CISF) Parveen Ranjan visited the project site to oversee the situation and get a first-hand report from officers on the previous evening’s fratricide.Police said Abhidesh and his wife Pooja, both head constables with CISF, were posted at the same Sewa-III project of the central PSU at Basohli—near the Himachal Pradesh border—but assigned different shifts. The unit administration had not allowed Pooja to enter or stay in the Quarter Guard area with her young child, aged about two-and-a-half.“While joining their respective shift at the site, either spouse would bring the toddler along to hand him over to the one heading home, despite being repeatedly warned against bringing the child to the project site. Even on Tuesday, one of them had brought the child to the site to hand over to the spouse, and someone complained about it to the Company Commander,” an officer said.“The complaint made to Assistant Commandant Ankit Kumar Pandey incensed the accused. In a fit of rage, Abhidesh walked into the Operations section office near the main gate and opened indiscriminate fire, killing Pandey, sub-inspector Lakshman Singh, and constables Sanjeev Kumar and Mohammed Rafiq,” the officer said.The attack wasn’t an isolated one among security personnel in this J&K zone under Jammu division. articles.title: Amaravati ORR to be built in four phases; civil works estimated to cost ₹10,596 crore
articles.summary: NHAI to build Amaravati Outer Ring Road in four phases: 190-km six-lane ORR plus 5.2-km spur; civil works ₹10,596 cr; 3 tunnels, 2 bridges.
articles.body: Vijayawada: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is all set to kick-start work on the outer ring road (ORR) for capital city Amaravati.The proposed ORR, envisaged as a six-lane high-speed road network encircling the capital region, will be executed in four packages covering nearly 190km. The Centre has estimated that civil works will cost ₹10,596 crore. The project, which also includes a 5.2-km four-lane spur connecting Narakoduru and Budampadu on the outskirts of Guntur, will have a cumulative construction length of 195.13km.NHAI has submitted detailed proposals, dividing the mega project into four operational packages, aimed at facilitating a phased execution of the strategically important road corridor. The overall project cost, including land acquisition and other components, has been estimated at ₹30,491 crore.The ORR alignment will include two major bridges across the Krishna river and three tunnels, reflecting the challenging terrain along parts of the proposed corridor. Package 1 will start at the 0-km point near Kanchikacherla in NTR district on the Vijayawada-Hyderabad highway and run through the Kondapalli and Pangidi forest areas up to the 27-km point near Mylavaram. NHAI has proposed two tunnels, 2.7km and 1.6km, on this stretch. The 930-m balance stretch between the 189-km and 189.93-km points has also been clubbed with this package.Similarly, package 2 will cover a 56-km stretch from the 27-km point to the 83-km point near Kolavennu in Kankipadu mandal of Krishna district.NHAI, in its DPR, said that package 3, covering 50.5km, will run from the 83-km point to Pulladigunta near Vatticherukuru mandal in Guntur district. It will also include the 5.2-km Narakoduru-Budampadu spur road and a 4.8-km bridge across the Krishna river near Valluripalem.According to NHAI-approved designs, package 4 will cover the remaining 55.5km from the 133.5-km point to the 189-km point near Kanchikacherla. It will feature a 400-m tunnel at Veerullapadu and a 3.15-km Krishna river bridge near Munnaluru. articles.body: Surat: Rising consumer awareness and a growing number of disputes, particularly involving insurance claims, have pushed consumer complaints in Surat to record levels, with the district consumer commission registering its highest-ever annual caseload in 2025.The Surat District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (Main) registered 1,885 cases in 2025, the highest in a single year. The year also recorded the highest number of disposals, with 1,179 cases decided.The trend continued in 2026. Between Jan and Sep, the commission registered 1,391 fresh cases and disposed of 1,053, placing it on course to approach last year’s figures.Data from the commission shows that 7,656 fresh complaints were filed between April 1, 2022, and Sep 30, 2026. In the same 54-month period, 5,015 cases were disposed of.The increase is striking when compared with the previous decade. Between 2012 and 2021, the commission registered 5,457 cases over 120 months, averaging about 45 cases a month. Since April 2022, the average has risen to 141 cases a month.Legal practitioners attribute the rise to greater consumer awareness and an increase in disputes involving insurance claim rejections and other consumer grievances.Consumer lawyer Shreyas Desai said: “The commission’s disposal rate has remained significant despite a steady rise in the number of consumer complaints. We have seen that the commission has taken up old cases first with the intention of disposal. articles.title: Sarna opposes new Gurdwara Act, warns against govt control
articles.summary: Paramjit Singh Sarna opposes calls for a new Sikh Gurdwaras Act, warning it could expand Centre or state control over SGPC and Sikh institutions.
articles.body: Amritsar: Paramjit Singh Sarna, the president of the Delhi unit of the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), on Wednesday opposed the demand for a new Sikh Gurdwaras Act, warning that changes to the existing legal framework could increase govt control over Sikh religious institutions.Sarna, a former president of the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee, was reacting to a resolution adopted at the International Sikh Confederation conclave in Chandigarh that called for consultations on preparing a new Punjab Sikh Gurdwaras Bill.He questioned why the issue of replacing the existing framework was raised at a conclave convened to discuss the SGPC elections. “The Panth cannot allow its hard-won control over historic gurdwaras to be surrendered through the back door in the name of reform,” Sarna said.Sarna alleged that the proposed change could ultimately give the Centre or state govts greater authority over the management of Sikh institutions.The SAD functionary said concerns regarding the functioning of Sikh institutions should be addressed through reforms within the Panth rather than by creating greater scope for govt intervention.The Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925, provides the statutory framework for the administration of specified Sikh gurdwaras and governs the functioning of the SGPC.The International Sikh Confederation conclave, held under the theme ‘The Way Forward: SGPC Elections’, had called on the Punjab govt to initiate consultations with the SGPC, Sikh legal experts and intellectuals for preparing a draft Punjab Sikh Gurdwaras Bill.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: Former California firefighter may have faked death to evade child sex abuse images charges, FBI says
articles.summary: The FBI is renewing its search for a former Alameda County firefighter who investigators believe may have faked his own death while facing federal charges on child sex abuse images.
articles.body: The FBI is renewing its search for a former Alameda County firefighter who investigators believe may have faked his own death while facing federal charges on child sex abuse images. Federal authorities announced Tuesday that the former firefighter may still be alive, prompting a new public appeal for information to help track him down. Charles Johnathen Harris was indicted by a federal grand jury in March 2023 for possession of child sex abuse images. Federal authorities said they received tips that he was allegedly uploading the material to social media while working at fire stations in Alameda County. At the time, Harris faced a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison and a fine of $250,000. However, a month after his indictment, Harris was believed to have drowned during a boating incident in Suisun Bay. Now, more than three years later, the FBI says there is a possibility that his drowning was staged. “There may have been tips that came into the FBI of a sighting of Mr. Harris; that is frequently the case, someone who has wanted to come forward to law enforcement,” said legal analyst Steven Clark. Clark noted that evading detection long-term remains a massive hurdle. “It’s very difficult now for someone to stay under the radar,” Clark said. “The feds are going to look for signs of life—has he communicated with relatives in any type of way?” Alameda County Fire officials told reporters they have no updates regarding their former employee. If Harris is indeed still alive, Clark warned that the legal fallout could easily spread to others. “Anyone harboring Mr. Harris or assisting him in anyway could face a federal felony of up to five years in prison,” Clark said. The FBI is asking anyone with information regarding Harris or his whereabouts to contact authorities immediately.
